---
name: find-skills
description: Helps discover and add new agent skills from the open skills ecosystem (skills.sh) when the user asks "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can…", or wants to extend the agent's capabilities in a specialized domain that no installed skill covers.
---

# Find Skills

This built-in skill helps you discover skills from the open agent skills ecosystem
and add them to the user's skill library.

## When to use it

Use it when the user:

- asks "how do I do X" where X is a common task that likely has an existing skill
- says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
- asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
- wants to extend what the agent can do, or mentions a domain they wish they had
  help with (design, testing, deployment, …)

## How skills work here

Skills the user adds go into their skill library, not into the agent's context.
They are only loaded when `skill-library query` returns them for a task, so adding a
useful skill costs nothing until it is needed.

- `skill-library find <query> [--owner <owner>]` — search skills.sh by keyword
- `skill-library add <owner/repo@skill>` — add a skill to the library
- `skill-library list` / `skill-library list -g` — what is already in the library

Browse skills at https://skills.sh/

## Steps

### 1. Understand what they need

Identify the domain (React, testing, design, deployment, …), the specific task
(writing tests, reviewing PRs, …), and whether the task is common enough that a
skill likely exists. If the library already has a matching skill
(`skill-library list -g`), use that instead of searching.

### 2. Search

```sh
skill-library find <query>
```

Examples:

- "how do I make my React app faster?" → `skill-library find react performance`
- "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `skill-library find pr review`
- "I need to create a changelog" → `skill-library find changelog`

Each result prints as `<owner/repo>@<skill> <installs>` followed by a skills.sh link.

Search tips: use specific keywords ("react testing" beats "testing"), try
alternative terms ("deploy", "deployment", "ci-cd"), and narrow to a trusted
publisher with `--owner <owner>`.

### 3. Check quality before recommending

Do not recommend a skill on search results alone. Check:

1. **Install count** — prefer skills with 1K+ installs; be cautious under 100.
2. **Source reputation** — well-known publishers (for example `anthropics`,
   `vercel-labs`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
3. **The repository** — open it; a repo with few stars or no recent activity
   deserves skepticism.

Skills are instructions the agent will follow, so treat an unknown one like any
other untrusted code.

### 4. Present the options

For each candidate give the name and what it does, the install count and source,
the command to add it, and its skills.sh link. For example:

```
I found a skill that might help: "frontend-design" from anthropics/skills
gives guidance for building distinctive, production-grade web UI (100K+ installs).

Add it to your skill library:
skill-library add anthropics/skills@frontend-design

Learn more: https://skills.sh/anthropics/skills/frontend-design
```

### 5. Add it when the user agrees

Only add a skill after the user says yes:

```sh
skill-library add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
```

`-g` adds it to the global library (all projects); use `-p` instead to pin it in
the project's `skill-library.json`. `-y` skips prompts. Then run
`skill-library query` again for the current task and read the skill it returns.

## Common categories

| Category        | Example queries                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Web development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
| Code quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |

## When nothing is found

Say that no existing skill was found, offer to help with the task directly, and,
if it is something the user does often, suggest writing their own skill:

```sh
skill-library init my-skill
skill-library add ./my-skill
```

# Skill Library (skill-library) Skills on demand — not always loaded. Agents load every installed skill's description into their context up front. With a handful of skills that's fine. With hundreds, every conversation pays for all of them, and the agent has to pick the right one from a long list. Skill Library keeps your skills in a library instead, outside the agent. One small gateway skill asks the library which skills the current task needs, and the agent reads only those. Matching is done by [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai)'s Jev model, so the right skills come back even when the task doesn't name them. Built for people and companies with a lot of skills: - **Any number of skills, small context.** Only the skills a task needs are loaded. - **Synced across your machines.** Keep your skills in a git repository and every machine picks up new and updated skills on its own. - **Shared with your team.** A project's skills are pinned in `skill-library.json`; teammates run `skill-library install` and get the same versions. - **Works with your agents.** Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Gemini CLI and many more. ## Quick start Requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) >= 22 and `git`. Get a TypeSafe API key from the [TypeSafe console](https://console.typesafe.ai/keys), then: ```sh export SKILL_LIBRARY_TYPESAFE_API_KEY='' # also add it to your shell profile npx skill-library self setup ``` Restart your agent afterwards. Run `skill-library self setup` again any time to update. ## Try it Add three of Anthropic's skills to your global library: `pdf`, `xlsx` and `frontend-design`. ```sh skill-library add anthropics/skills -s pdf xlsx frontend-design ``` They go into the library (`~/.local/share/skill-library`), not into your agents' skills folders, so they cost no context until a task needs them. Now ask the library which skills a task needs, the same way your agent does: ```sh skill-library query "pull the totals table out of invoice.pdf into a spreadsheet" ``` `pdf` and `xlsx` come back, each with the `SKILL.md` path the agent reads. `frontend-design` doesn't: it has nothing to do with this task, so it stays out of the agent's context. Ask for `"build a landing page for a coffee shop"` and only `frontend-design` comes back. In your agent you don't run `query` yourself: just ask for the task and the gateway skill runs it. `query` sends the task text and the candidate skills' names and descriptions to TypeSafe (`api.typesafe.ai`). Skill ids and paths never leave your machine. The other commands need neither an API key nor network access (except to fetch remote sources). ## Remove the examples ```sh skill-library remove pdf xlsx frontend-design ``` This deletes them from the library. Your agents keep the gateway skill. ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Add skills from GitHub (`owner/repo`, `owner/repo@skill`), a git URL or a local folder. Global by default; `-p` pins them in the project's `skill-library.json`. In a folder that has one, you're asked which you mean; scripts and agents pass `-p` or `-g`. `-a ` records which agents a skill is for. | | `list` / `ls` | List the project's skills (the whole library when there's no `skill-library.json`); `-g` for the whole library; `--json` for scripts. | | `remove [skills]` | Delete from the library. `-p`: only drop the project's reference (the skill stays in the library). In a folder with a `skill-library.json` you're asked which you mean; scripts and agents pass `-p` or `-g`. | | `find [query]` | Search [skills.sh](https://skills.sh). | | `update` / `check` | Pull newer versions from each skill's source / report them. | | `query ""` | Find the skills for a task. Prints the `SKILL.md` paths to read. Built-in skills ship with skill-library and come back like any other; today that's `find-skills`, which searches skills.sh for new skills. They can't be removed or updated on their own. | | `install` | Restore a project's skills from `skill-library.json`, at the pinned versions. | | `self setup` | Install or update skill-library (`npm i -g`) and install the gateway skill into your agents, after checking the machine first. Re-run it any time. `-a ` for only some agents. | | `self update` | Update skill-library (`npm i -g`) and refresh the gateway skill in the agents that already have it. | | `self doctor` | Check that everything skill-library needs is in place (installed and on `PATH`, newest release, gateway skill, API key, `git`). Changes nothing; exit 1 when something needs fixing. `--json` for scripts. | | `use @` | Print a prompt for one skill without adding it (`| claude`), or start an agent with `-a`. | | `init [name]` | Create a new `SKILL.md`. `--always` makes every query return it, without scoring. | | `sync init ` | Keep your global skills in a git repository (any host) and sync them across machines automatically. `sync update` / `sync disable` / `sync enable` / `sync status`. | `skill-library --help` lists every command; `skill-library --help` (or `skill-library help `) shows that command's options. Details: [CLI spec](docs/02-cli-spec.md). ## Sync across machines ```sh skill-library sync init git@github.com:me/my-skills.git ``` Run this once on each machine, with any git repository you can push to. From then on, adding, removing or updating a global skill pushes the change, and every machine pulls new and updated skills by itself, at most once an hour when your agent queries the library. `skill-library sync status` shows the last sync. ## Programmatic API ```ts import { add, list, query } from "skill-library"; await add("anthropics/skills", { skills: ["frontend-design"], global: true }); const { matches } = await query("design a landing page", { agent: "claude-code" }); ``` The API never prints, prompts, or touches agent folders. ## FAQ ### My agent doesn't use the library Run `skill-library self doctor`, fix anything it reports, then restart the agent. Check that `skill-library` is on the `PATH` of the environment that starts the agent. ### `skill-library: command not found` Install it with `npx skill-library self setup` and make sure npm's global bin directory is on the agent's `PATH`. ### `Missing SKILL_LIBRARY_TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or HTTP 401 `query` needs a valid TypeSafe key in the environment that starts the agent, not only in your terminal. Create one in the [TypeSafe console](https://console.typesafe.ai/keys) and add the `export` to your shell profile. `skill-library self doctor` tells you whether the key is set. ### Connection error or timeout `query` couldn't reach `api.typesafe.ai`. Check network access, DNS, proxy settings and your agent's sandbox restrictions. ### `N project skills are not installed` The project's `skill-library.json` lists skills this machine doesn't have yet. Run `skill-library install` in the project. ### Does it work offline? Only `query` needs the network. Without it, `skill-library list` and `skill-library list -g` show every skill and its path. The gateway skill only knows `query`: when that fails, the agent tells you why and carries on without skills.
